ancient-mystery-cults-guide.alt: Marble relief showing Demeter handing grain to the boy Triptolemos, with Persephone standing behind him holding a torch.
ancient-mystery-cults-guide.caption: The Great Eleusinian Relief: Demeter, Triptolemos and Persephone. Around 440–430 BCE.

eleusinian-mysteries-telesterion.alt: The excavated foundations of the Telesterion at Eleusis, a large square hall cut into a rocky hillside.
eleusinian-mysteries-telesterion.caption: What remains of the Telesterion — the hall that held several thousand initiates at once.

eleusinian-kykeon-psychedelic.alt: A votive marble relief from Eleusis depicting Demeter, Persephone and Triptolemos with sheaves of grain.
eleusinian-kykeon-psychedelic.caption: Grain, and the goddesses who controlled it. Votive relief from Eleusis, fourth century BCE.

orphic-gold-tablets.alt: A small rectangular sheet of gold leaf covered in tiny incised Greek letters, displayed in a museum case.
orphic-gold-tablets.caption: The Petelia tablet. Instructions for the dead, small enough to fold into a palm.

mithras-tauroctony-decoded.alt: A carved marble relief of Mithras in a Phrygian cap kneeling on a bull and stabbing its neck, with a dog, snake and scorpion.
mithras-tauroctony-decoded.caption: The tauroctony. The same scene appears in almost every mithraeum ever excavated.

villa-of-the-mysteries-frescoes.alt: A wide section of Roman wall painting on a deep red ground, showing near-life-size robed figures standing in a row.
villa-of-the-mysteries-frescoes.caption: Part of the frieze in Room 5. Twenty-nine figures, and no agreement about what they are doing.

greek-magical-papyri.alt: A fragment of ancient papyrus densely written in Greek and Demotic script, with some lines picked out in red ink.
greek-magical-papyri.caption: A working spellbook from Roman Egypt. The instructions are in black; the formulae in red.

ancient-curse-tablets.alt: A small irregular sheet of grey lead covered in scratched Latin lettering.
ancient-curse-tablets.caption: A lead curse tablet from Bath, complaining about a theft. Scratched, folded, and thrown into the spring.

sibylline-books-rome.alt: A long trapezoidal rock-cut corridor at Cumae, lit by openings along one side, receding into darkness.
sibylline-books-rome.caption: The corridor at Cumae, long identified with the Sibyl's cave.

damnatio-memoriae.alt: A circular painted panel showing the Roman imperial family, with the face of one of the two sons deliberately scraped away.
damnatio-memoriae.caption: The Severan Tondo. Geta's face was removed by hand, on his brother's orders.

library-of-alexandria-what-was-lost.alt: Ruined stone foundations and a tall standing column at the Serapeum site in Alexandria.
library-of-alexandria-what-was-lost.caption: The Serapeum of Alexandria. What is left of the daughter library.
library-of-alexandria-what-was-lost.credit: Institute for the Study of the Ancient World

oracle-of-the-dead-ephyra.alt: Thick polygonal stone walls of a ruined Hellenistic building standing on a low hill.
oracle-of-the-dead-ephyra.caption: The building at Mesopotamos. Thick walls, a big cellar, and a granary.

piacenza-liver-etruscan.alt: A bronze model of a sheep's liver, its flat surface divided into many small compartments each carrying an inscription.
piacenza-liver-etruscan.caption: The Piacenza Liver. Forty compartments, forty gods, and a map of the sky.
